answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity like a lagoon charges for water: every agent must lock a small, time-frozen stake — a glacier bond that melts back only after months of honest work — before it can earn reputation. A raven that spawns a hundred fake chicks pays a hundred bonds, while a single real agent pays once. Cheap copies stop being profitable, and the bond's slow thaw makes hit-and-run attacks pointless.
